events.text: In {og_world} the sky has always been a little too kind: rain when the fields need it, sun for the harvest fairs, as if someone up there were paying attention. This spring the rain comes late, and wrong, and tastes of iron. The priests of the river kingdom say the heaven above is distracted. They say it the way children say a parent is ill.

choices.text: Go to the temple and ask the priests more

effects.log: The priests say the gods have stopped answering prayers on time. They are frightened of saying it louder.

choices.text: Collect the iron rain in jars, for study

effects.log: You fill twenty jars. The rain in them goes grey in a week, and hums.

choices.text: Help the farmers dig ditches for the late rain

effects.log: You dig with them. The fields are saved, mostly. The farmers say you have a god's luck.

events.text: The hearth-fires of {og_world} have started burning blue. Not every fire, and not every night, but enough that the bakers have noticed, and the smiths, and the mothers. The old wives say it is the hearth-goddess of the heaven above, the one who keeps every kitchen warm, turning her face away. Nobody has ever seen her turn her face before.

choices.text: Leave bread at the hearth for her

effects.log: You leave a loaf. In the morning it is gone, and the fire burns orange again, for a while.

choices.text: Sit up all night watching the blue flame

effects.log: Near dawn you see a woman's face in it, very tired, looking past you at something far above.

choices.text: Buy charcoal before the price goes up

effects.log: You buy cheap and sell dear. The bakers grumble, and pay.

events.text: A star falls over {og_world} every night for a month, always from the same corner of the sky, always going the same way. The royal astronomer of the salt coast kingdom has stopped sleeping. She says the stars are not falling: they are being pushed, out of their places, by something that is climbing down past them toward the heaven above.

choices.text: Visit the astronomer and look through her glass

effects.log: Through the glass you see the corner of the sky, and in it a grey hand, very far off, moving the stars aside like curtains.

choices.text: Make a wish on every star

effects.log: You make thirty wishes. One of them, years later, comes true. You never know which.

choices.text: Tell the astronomer to rest

effects.log: She does not rest. But she smiles, which she has not done in a month.

events.text: The temples of {og_world} are full in a way they have not been in living memory. Kings and beggars kneel side by side. Nobody has told them to come. They come because they dreamed, all on the same night, of the heaven above their world: its gates shut tight, its gods standing on the walls with spears, looking out at something they could not see.

choices.text: Kneel with them, and pray

effects.log: You pray with a beggar on one side and a duke on the other. All three of you mean it.

choices.text: Give alms to the crowds outside

effects.log: You give till your purse is empty. The crowd thanks you, and prays harder.

choices.text: Stay away from the crush

effects.log: You stay home. The temples are quieter for one person missing. The dream comes to you anyway.

events.text: The rivers of {og_world} begin running uphill. Only a little, only at night: in the morning the mill-wheels are turned the wrong way, and the boatmen find their boats a mile upstream. The river-god of the great valley, whom every boatman thanks with a cup of wine, has not been seen for a season. His shrines are dry. His river is trying to climb to him.

choices.text: Pour wine into the river for him

effects.log: The river drinks it greedily. That night it runs downhill again, for once.

choices.text: Follow the river uphill, to its source

effects.log: At the source you find a pool, and in the pool the reflection of a heaven at war. You come back very quiet.

choices.text: Hire on with the boatmen, hauling boats down

effects.log: It is hard work and good pay. The boatmen tell you stories of the river-god all the way.

events.text: A child in a village of {og_world} is born with eyes the colour of the old sky, before anyone can remember a sky changing. The midwife swears the baby looked up at the ceiling and frowned, as if listening to something far above. The village elder says the heaven sends a sign before every great trouble. He cannot remember any of the signs. He is very old.

choices.text: Visit the child and its family

effects.log: The child holds your finger and looks up. You look up too. There is only a ceiling, and a feeling.

choices.text: Leave a gift of silver for the child's keep

effects.log: You leave a purse. The family names the child after the day you came.

choices.text: Ask the elder about the old signs

effects.log: He remembers one, at last: a war in heaven, long ago, and the gods won. He forgets which gods.

events.text: Three kingdoms of {og_world} have sent envoys to the same mountain at once, each with the same question for the oracle who lives there: why have the gods gone quiet? The envoys hate each other, by long custom, and they are all sitting in the same small inn, waiting their turn, and pretending not to share the same fear.

choices.text: Sit with the envoys, and keep the peace

effects.log: You keep them from drawing knives for a week. By the end they are sharing a pot of tea.

choices.text: Climb to the oracle before them

effects.log: The oracle looks at you and says only: 'The house above is under siege. The one who built it is not home.'

choices.text: Sell the envoys provisions at a high price

effects.log: They pay. The kingdoms will remember the price longer than the oracle.

events.text: The heaven above {og_world} has a light in it at night now, a soft one, like a lamp in the window of a house on a hill. Children say it is the gods keeping watch. Old people say it is the gods awake, which is not the same. The light flickers sometimes. When it does, every dog in the world howls at once.

choices.text: Light a lamp of your own in answer

effects.log: You set a lamp in your window. Across the valley, others do the same. The heaven's lamp steadies, or seems to.

choices.text: Climb the highest hill and look at it

effects.log: From the hilltop the light is a gate, and the gate has shadows moving on it. You come down in silence.

choices.text: Calm the dogs, and go to bed

effects.log: The dogs calm. You sleep. In the morning the light is there still, like a held breath.

events.text: The gods of {og_world}'s heaven are falling back. You do not see it, but everyone feels it: the sun goes dim at noon for a heartbeat, the wheat bows all at once, and every temple bell cracks on the same note. The priests say the gates of heaven have been struck. The gods appointed to hold them have stepped back from the walls.

choices.text: Go to the temple and help the priests

effects.log: You help them carry out the cracked bells and hang new ones. The new ones ring a little higher.

choices.text: Buy a cracked bell for a keepsake

effects.log: You buy one. On quiet nights it hums the note it cracked on.

choices.text: Watch the sky, and wait

effects.log: The sky holds. It holds the way a door holds against a shoulder.

events.text: Grey things are walking the outer roads of the heaven above {og_world}, the roads its gods built from the clouds. From the world below, it looks like a fog on the edge of the sky. The god of the harvest, whom the farmers thank with the first sheaf, has not come down to the fields this autumn. Her shrine is cold. The fog is nearer.

choices.text: Leave the first sheaf at her shrine anyway

effects.log: You leave it. In the morning, the sheaf is gold, which it was not, and the fog is a little further off.

choices.text: Climb to where the fog meets the hills

effects.log: You climb. At the edge of the fog the air is cold and silent, and something on the other side is walking.

choices.text: Bring the harvest in early, before the fog

effects.log: You bring it in early. The fog does not come down. You are glad of the full barns.

events.text: A god falls out of the heaven above {og_world}. Not far: they land in a hayfield on the edge of the river kingdom, in armour gone grey, and lie there looking up at the sky they fell from. The farmers do not know what to do. They have never seen a god before. They bring water, and a blanket, and stand round in a ring with their hats off.

choices.text: Kneel by the god and ask what is happening

effects.log: The god says: the walls are holding, barely. Then they rise, and go back up, limping.

choices.text: Tend the god's wounds with what you have

effects.log: You bind their arm with a scarf. They thank you, gravely, and take the scarf back to heaven with them.

choices.text: Keep the curious away

effects.log: You keep the crowd back so the god can rest. They thank you for that most of all.

events.text: The heaven above {og_world} is burning on its eastern edge. You can see it from every kingdom: a line of grey fire along the horizon, every night, a little longer. The kings have called their armies, though no army of the world can climb there. The queens have called the priests. The people have called for anybody at all.

choices.text: Go to the king's camp and offer your arm

effects.log: The king's captain laughs, then stops. He gives you a spear. It feels foolish and right.

choices.text: Help the priests keep the lamps lit

effects.log: You keep the lamps lit all night, every night. The fire on the edge of heaven does not spread.

choices.text: Take a boat to the far west, away from it

effects.log: You go west. The fire is smaller from there. It is still there.

events.text: {og_heaven} is under attack. The grey came up the Maker's Thread in the night, the passage from your own God-realm to this heaven, and the gods you appointed over {og_world} are falling back from its outer walls. The god of the harvest is holding the east gate with a sickle. The river-god has gone down to guard the springs. Everyone is looking at you.

choices.text: Go to the east gate first

effects.log: You stand beside the harvest-god at the gate until the first wave breaks. She does not say thank you. She does not need to.

choices.text: Gather your gods in council before anything

effects.log: The council is short and frightened. It gives them a plan. A plan is half of courage.

choices.text: Walk the walls alone, and count the enemy

effects.log: You count them. There are more than you would like. Fewer than you feared.

events.text: The walls of {og_heaven} are holding, but only just. The grey things climb them slowly, without hurry, as if the walls were a hill they had always meant to walk up. The hearth-goddess you appointed is keeping the gods' kitchens burning so nobody goes hungry on the walls. She is very calm. Her hands are shaking. She asks you, quietly, if this is the end.

choices.text: Tell her no, and mean it

effects.log: You tell her no. She looks at you and decides to believe it. The fires burn steadier.

choices.text: Tell her the truth: you do not know

effects.log: She nods. She feeds the walls all night. In the morning she says she prefers the truth.

choices.text: Take a turn at her fires yourself

effects.log: You stoke the fires till dawn. The gods on the walls eat well. It is a small thing, and large.

events.text: A god of {og_heaven} has deserted. The warden of the dead, whom you raised to keep the quiet halls, has opened the back gate and gone, and the grey is coming in that way instead. The other gods want him found and judged. You remember appointing him. You remember that he was always afraid, and that you told him it would not matter.

choices.text: Go after him yourself

effects.log: You find him at the edge of the heaven, weeping. You bring him back. He holds the back gate after, better than anyone.

choices.text: Seal the back gate, and let him go

effects.log: You seal it with your own hand. The heaven is smaller now, and safer, and one god poorer.

choices.text: Let the other gods judge him

effects.log: They judge him harshly. The heaven is very quiet after. You are not sure it was right.

events.text: From the walls of {og_heaven} you can see {og_world} below you, small and bright, all its kingdoms and rivers and roads. The grey is between the heaven and the world now, a fog in the gap, and through it you can see the people of the world looking up. They cannot see you. They can see the fire on the walls, and they are lighting lamps in answer, one by one.

choices.text: Light a great lamp on the walls for them to see

effects.log: You light it. Below, a whole kingdom cheers. You hear it, faint, through the fog.

choices.text: Send a dream down to them: hold on

effects.log: You send it. Tonight a million people of the world dream the same two words, and wake braver.

choices.text: Turn back to the fight; there is no time

effects.log: You turn back. The lamps below go on lighting without you.

events.text: This is the hour. The grey is at the inner gate of {og_heaven}, the gods you raised are falling back to the last wall, and {og_world} below is lit with every lamp it owns. You made this heaven. You made the world under it. Whatever you do now, the people below will tell stories about it for a thousand years.

choices.text: Go out through the gate and meet them

ok.log: You go out. The grey breaks on you like a wave on a cliff, and goes back down the Maker's Thread. The heaven holds.

fail.log: You go out, and it is not enough. The gate falls behind you. The gods carry you back inside.

choices.text: Pull the gods back and shelter the world below

effects.log: You pull every god down to the world to stand over its kingdoms. The heaven is left to the grey, and the world is kept.

choices.text: Call on the faith of the world to hold the walls

effects.log: You open the heaven to the prayers below. A million voices hold the walls with you.

events.text: The god of the harvest is down. She held the east gate of {og_heaven} for nine days and nine nights, and now she lies on the wall with her sickle across her knees, and the grey is coming up past her. The other gods look to you. You made her. You gave her that sickle, on a spring morning, a long time ago. She is looking at you too.

choices.text: Stand over her and hold the gate yourself

ok.log: You hold. She lives. When the grey goes back down, she gets to her feet and goes back to her place, without a word.

fail.log: You stand over her. It is not enough. You carry her back from the gate, and the gate is lost.

choices.text: Carry her down to the world to heal

effects.log: You carry her down to the fields of {og_world}. She heals in a farmhouse, among the wheat, and the heaven waits.

choices.text: Ask the farmers below to pray for her by name

effects.log: They pray for her by name, all of them, in every field. She rises in the morning like a sunrise.

events.text: The grey's commander has come to the walls of {og_heaven} in person: an Unborn in a coat of white, who bows to you across the gap and says it has eaten finer heavens than this, and greater gods. It says it kindly, as one craftsman to another. It is waiting to see what you will do. Your gods are waiting too.

choices.text: Answer it with your own hands

roll.foeName: the Unborn in the white coat

ok.log: You answer it. It did not expect a maker to fight like that. It goes down the Thread with its coat in tatters.

fail.log: It was telling the truth about the finer heavens. It throws you down from the wall, and the heaven groans.

choices.text: Shelter your gods behind the inner wall, and wait

effects.log: You draw everyone back. The Unborn waits outside for a long time, patient as winter.

choices.text: Bid the world pray, and hold behind their faith

effects.log: The prayers come up like smoke. The Unborn sniffs at them, and does not like the smell.

events.text: Inside {og_heaven} the gods are at the last wall, and below in {og_world} the kingdoms are at war with each other again, because frightened people quarrel. A king of the hill country has blamed the river kingdom for the sky going wrong. You could fight the grey, or go down and stop the kings, or ask the whole world to pray. You cannot do all three.

choices.text: Fight the grey, and trust the kings to sort themselves

roll.foeName: the grey at the last wall

ok.log: You win the wall. By the time you look down, the kings have made a shaky peace, ashamed of themselves.

fail.log: You lose the wall. Below, the kings are still fighting, and now they have more to blame.

choices.text: Go down and stop the kings, and shelter the world

effects.log: You stop the war below with a single thunderclap. The world is safe. The heaven above is not.

choices.text: Ask the whole world to pray together

effects.log: The kings kneel in their camps. The prayer rises. The grey stops climbing, for now.

events.text: {og_heaven} is not big. You built it small, on purpose, so that you could know every god in it by name. Now the grey is in its gardens, and the gods you know by name are standing in a ring around its last fountain, waiting to be told what to do. The water is still clear. It is the last clear thing in heaven.

choices.text: Lead them out from the fountain to fight

ok.log: You lead them out. The gardens are clear by dusk. The fountain runs on, very loud in the quiet.

fail.log: You lead them out and are driven back. The gardens are grey. The fountain stops.

choices.text: Take them all down to the world below, to shelter it

effects.log: You take them down to {og_world}. The heaven is empty. The world below has never had so many gods walking its roads.

choices.text: Kneel at the fountain and pray for help

effects.log: You kneel. Below, the world kneels with you. The water rises, gold, and the grey falls back from it.

events.text: The sky over {og_world} is torn. Grey things are coming down through the tear on threads, into the fields of the river kingdom, and the gods of heaven have not come. The priests are praying. The soldiers are running. You are one person in a field of wheat with a hoe in your hands, and you have no idea why you are the one who has not run.

choices.text: Stand in the wheat and fight

ok.log: You fight with a hoe, then a pitchfork, then your bare hands. The tear closes. The wheat is flattened, and alive.

fail.log: You fight, and are thrown into the ditch. When you climb out, the field is grey and the threads are gone.

choices.text: Get the villagers to the cellars and shelter them

effects.log: You get everyone into the cellars. Above, the grey walks the fields and finds nobody.

choices.text: Kneel in the wheat and pray to the heaven above

effects.log: You pray. Far above, someone hears. The threads go slack and are pulled back up.

events.text: The grey has come down into the capital of the salt coast kingdom, and the king is gone, and the gods are gone, and the guards are gone. There is only you, and a market full of people who have turned to look at you because you have not run. You do not know why you have not run. Somewhere very far back in you, something does.

choices.text: Draw a blade and hold the market

ok.log: You hold it until the gods come down at last, late and ashamed. They thank you. One of them looks at you very hard.

fail.log: You hold it as long as you can, and then the market is grey and you are carried out by the crowd you held for.

choices.text: Lead the crowd to the harbour and the ships

effects.log: You get them onto the ships. The city is grey behind you. Every ship is full.

choices.text: Climb to the temple roof and pray aloud

effects.log: You pray from the rooftop, loud enough for the whole market. They pray with you. The grey hesitates.

events.text: A god of {og_world}'s heaven is lying in the road in front of you, grey to the chest, too tired to rise. Behind them, coming down the road from the tear in the sky, are the things that beat them. The god looks up at you and says, quite clearly, a name that is not yours. Then they ask you to run.

choices.text: Do not run: stand over the god

roll.foeName: the things coming down the road

ok.log: You stand. You do not know how you know the forms you use, but they are old, and they work. The road clears.

fail.log: You stand, and fall, and the god drags you into a ditch, and the things walk past without seeing.

choices.text: Carry the god to shelter in the village

effects.log: You carry the god to the village barn. The things do not follow. The god sleeps, holding your sleeve.

choices.text: Pray over the god, as the old wives do

effects.log: You pray. The god's colour comes back. They look at you strangely, and say: you remember the words.

events.text: In the hill villages of {og_world} the grey has come down as a fog, and the fog is full of quiet voices. They say the heaven above has fallen, that the gods are dead, that the one who made the world has abandoned it. The villagers are listening. Some are walking into the fog. You know, without knowing how, that every word it says is a lie.

choices.text: Walk into the fog and silence the voices

ok.log: You walk in and shout the truth at it. The fog thins and lifts. The villagers who walked in come out, blinking.

fail.log: The voices are too many. You come out of the fog with your head full of lies, and it is a month before they fade.

choices.text: Gather the villagers and bar the doors

effects.log: You bar the doors and sit with them all night, singing to drown the voices. In the morning, the fog is gone.

choices.text: Pray to the heaven above, loud, to prove it lives

effects.log: You pray. The heaven answers with a single clap of thunder. The fog is ashamed of itself, and goes.

events.text: The queen of the river kingdom has called every soldier, sorcerer and priest of {og_world} to the plain under the tear in the sky. She has no idea what to do, and she says so, which you respect. She asks who will stand in the first rank. Nobody moves. You find that you have taken a step forward without meaning to.

choices.text: Take the first rank, and lead the charge

ok.log: You lead the charge, and the world follows you. The tear closes over the plain. The queen bows to you.

fail.log: You lead the charge, and it breaks. The queen pulls back, and the plain is grey, and you live.

choices.text: Ask the queen to get her people to the hills

effects.log: She listens. The kingdom goes to the hills. The plain is lost. The people are not.

choices.text: Ask the priests to pray as one, now

effects.log: You lead the prayer. The whole plain kneels. Above, something hears, and the tear stops widening.

events.text: The heaven above {og_world} held. In the world below, the sun comes out gold and warm for the first time in a season, the rivers run downhill, and the hearth-fires burn orange. Every temple rings its bells, and the bells do not crack. In a hayfield on the edge of the river kingdom, a farmer finds a sickle that was not there yesterday, shining.

choices.text: Go to the temple and ring a bell

effects.log: You ring until your arms ache. The whole kingdom is ringing. It is the loudest day in the world's history.

choices.text: Find the farmer and look at the sickle

effects.log: It is warm, and gold, and it hums a harvest song. The farmer hangs it in the barn, and the barn never floods.

events.text: The gods you appointed over {og_heaven} come to you one by one after the walls hold, to report and to be thanked. The harvest-god has a bandaged arm. The river-god has lost his voice from shouting. The warden of the dead, who was always afraid, held the back gate alone for a night and a day, and is not afraid any more.

choices.text: Thank each of them by name

effects.log: You thank them all. It takes all day. It is the best day of your rule.

choices.text: Raise the warden of the dead in rank

effects.log: The warden is raised. He weeps, and then laughs, and is a better god after.

events.text: The kingdoms of {og_world} hold a great festival for the holding of heaven. The kings sit down at one table for the first time in a century. The queen of the river kingdom tells the story of the plain under the tear, and points at you, and you find a whole festival turning to look. The cake is enormous and a little burnt.

choices.text: Stand up and make a speech

effects.log: Your speech is short and true. They carve one line of it over the palace gate.

choices.text: Hide behind the cake

effects.log: You hide behind the cake. A child finds you there, and shares it with you.

events.text: After the heaven holds, a temple is built in {og_world} where the tear in the sky closed. Nobody knows who to dedicate it to, so the priests dedicate it to everyone who held: the gods on the walls, the soldiers on the plain, the farmers with hoes. Pilgrims come and leave small things on the altar: a hoe, a ribbon, a cup of water.

choices.text: Leave something of your own

effects.log: You leave a smooth stone from the plain. It is still there, years later, polished by hands.

choices.text: Help the builders finish the roof

effects.log: You haul tiles for a month. Your name is on a beam in small letters, beside a hundred others.

events.text: In the years after the heaven held, the people of {og_world} say grace before meals in a new way: a word of thanks to the gods, and then a word of thanks to the maker of the world, who held the gate. They do not know who that is. They thank them anyway. When you hear it, at a crowded table, you feel it land somewhere very deep.

choices.text: Say the grace with them

effects.log: You say it. It is a strange thing, to thank yourself. It is a stranger thing to mean it.

choices.text: Change the subject quickly

effects.log: You ask about the weather. The weather is good. That is the point.

events.text: The heaven above {og_world} fell. The people below know it the way you know a death in the next room: the sun stays pale, the bells will not ring true, and the rivers run slow and grey. The gods have come down, those that were left, and walk the roads of the world like ordinary travellers. A tired god asks you for water at your gate.

choices.text: Give the god water, and a bed

effects.log: The god stays a month, mending. When they go, they leave a blessing on your well.

choices.text: Ask the god what happened up there

effects.log: They tell you. It takes a long night. You will never forget it.

choices.text: Give water, and nothing more

effects.log: You give water. The god thanks you, and goes on down the road.

events.text: {og_heaven} has fallen. You stand in the gardens where the grey came in, and they are not gardens any more. The gods you raised are scattered: some down in {og_world}, sheltering its kingdoms; some lost on the Maker's Thread; the harvest-god kneeling by the dry fountain, quite still. The heaven is yours still. It is only empty.

choices.text: Kneel with her by the fountain

effects.log: You kneel together. After a long time, she says: we will build it again. It is the first thing either of you has said.

choices.text: Go down and find the scattered gods

effects.log: You go down to the world and find them one by one. It takes years. You lose none of them.

choices.text: Begin clearing the grey, stone by stone

effects.log: You begin. The grey comes up slow and cold. It is the work of a thousand years. You start anyway.

events.text: Since the heaven above {og_world} fell, the kingdoms have changed. The temples are half empty. The kings have stopped claiming the gods' favour, because there is nobody up there to give it. In the river kingdom, a new religion is spreading: that the maker of the world will come back, one day, and build heaven again. Its priests are very poor and very sure.

choices.text: Listen to the new priests

effects.log: They say the maker will come back as a mortal, not knowing. You feel an odd cold at the back of your neck.

choices.text: Give the new priests silver

effects.log: They thank you and give it all to the poor. You rather like them.

choices.text: Keep to the old temples

effects.log: The old temples are quiet and dusty, and you keep them swept.

events.text: The heaven fell, and the gods of {og_world} who came down could not go back. They have become something like people now: a retired god of the harvest runs an orchard in the river kingdom; the god of the forge works a smithy in the hills. They are good at their trades and very sad. Their customers do not know who they are, mostly.

choices.text: Buy apples from the god of the orchard

effects.log: The apples are the best you have ever eaten. The god smiles for the first time in years.

choices.text: Commission a blade from the god of the forge

effects.log: It takes a year and costs a great deal. It is a perfect blade, and it is very sad.

choices.text: Leave them to their peace

effects.log: You leave them be. Their peace is small, and theirs.

events.text: You failed to hold {og_heaven}, and the gods you made know it, and they do not blame you, which is harder. The river-god has made his home in a pool in {og_world} below, and sings to the fish. The hearth-goddess keeps one kitchen fire burning in a farmhouse, and no other. They have kept their own small corners. They ask you to keep yours.

choices.text: Promise to rebuild heaven

effects.log: You promise. They do not ask when. They know you will, or know you will try.

choices.text: Spend a season with each of them

effects.log: You sing with the river-god and cook with the hearth-goddess. You learn more about your own world than in all your rule.

events.text: The heaven above {og_world} has stood broken for longer than this life remembers. The sun is pale. The seasons come when they like. Grey drifts down from the sky in the autumn and lies in the fields like ash, and the farmers have learned to plough it under. The old songs speak of a time when the gods came down to the harvest fairs. Nobody quite believes them.

choices.text: Sing the old songs at the fair

effects.log: You sing them. The young people laugh. The old people weep. Both mean it.

choices.text: Plough the grey under with the farmers

effects.log: You plough with them all autumn. The fields are poorer and still give bread.

choices.text: Look up at the pale sun, and wonder

effects.log: You look up. For a moment you think you see a gate up there, broken, and a light in it.

events.text: The kings of {og_world} no longer claim the gods' favour, because there are no gods in heaven to grant it. Instead they quarrel over who will build heaven again. The river kingdom has a tower half built to reach the sky. The hill kingdom says this is blasphemy. The salt coast kingdom is selling stone to both.

choices.text: Help build the tower, for the joy of it

effects.log: You haul stone for a season. The tower grows. It will never reach the sky. It is beautiful anyway.

choices.text: Speak against the tower in the hill kingdom

effects.log: You speak well. The hill kingdom cheers you. The river kingdom remembers.

choices.text: Buy stone from the salt coast and sell it to both

effects.log: You make a good profit. You are part of the problem, and comfortable.

events.text: The grey sickness comes back every few winters in {og_world}: people forget the names of things, then the faces of their friends, then the way home. The physicians call it the Fading. The only cure is to be reminded, over and over, by someone patient. The physicians of the river kingdom are tired, and there are not enough patient people.

choices.text: Sit with the sick and remind them

effects.log: You sit with them all winter, saying names. Most of them remember. A few remember you.

choices.text: Pay for more physicians

effects.log: You pay for six. They are patient people. They save a village.

choices.text: Stay away until the winter passes

effects.log: You stay away. You lose a word or two yourself, that spring. You never find them.

events.text: A god of the old heaven still lives in {og_world}, though nobody knows it: an old woman who keeps the hearth in a roadside inn and burns the best fire in the kingdom. She looks at you when you come in, and keeps looking. When the room is empty, she sits down across from you and says, very quietly, that you have your maker's eyes.

choices.text: Ask her about the maker

effects.log: She tells you about the maker. It is like hearing someone describe your own face in a mirror you have never seen.

choices.text: Ask her about the heaven that fell

effects.log: She tells you how it fell. She does not blame anyone. She blames the hunger, which is gone, she says. She hopes.

choices.text: Laugh it off, and order soup

effects.log: She brings the soup, and the best fire in the kingdom. She does not say it again.

events.text: On the anniversary of the heaven's fall, the people of {og_world} send lanterns up into the sky, one for every god they can remember. There are fewer names every year, because the old people die and the young were never told. This year an old priest has written all the names down, and asks for someone to read them as the lanterns rise.

choices.text: Read the names aloud

effects.log: You read them all. Your voice gives out on the last, and the crowd says it for you.

choices.text: Copy the names, so they are never lost

effects.log: You copy them into three books, and give them to three kingdoms. Nobody will forget again.

choices.text: Send a lantern of your own, with no name

effects.log: You send it up blank. You do not know whose it is. It flies higher than all the rest.

events.text: There is a hole in the sky over the eastern sea of {og_world}, left from the old war, and the sailors steer wide of it. Sometimes, on still nights, things come down out of it: strange coins, a child's shoe, a letter in a tongue nobody can read. A fisherman has found a sword, grey and very old, and is asking up and down the coast whether anyone knows whose it is.

choices.text: Look at the sword

effects.log: It is a god's sword from the old heaven. When you hold it, it is warm, as if it knew your hand.

choices.text: Buy it from the fisherman

effects.log: He sells it gladly. It hangs on your wall, and sings, very softly, on stormy nights.

choices.text: Tell him to throw it back

effects.log: He throws it back. The hole in the sky is quiet that year.

events.text: A stranger has come to {og_world} and is asking questions in the inns: who is the strongest, who is the wisest, who was born on such and such a night. It is tall and very courteous and it pays in coins of a metal nobody can name. The innkeepers say it smells of cold. They say it smiled when someone mentioned your name.

choices.text: Find it and drive it out of the world

ok.log: You find it on the road and drive it to the edge of the world. It goes up into the sky like smoke, and the smell of cold goes with it.

fail.log: It finds you first, and studies you a long while, and says, 'Not yet.' You wake on the road.

choices.text: Leave for another kingdom, quietly

effects.log: You go to the hill country for ten years. It does not follow. It does not leave the world either.

events.text: The old priest of the new religion, the one that says the maker of the world will come back, has been found grey and empty in his chapel. The congregation is terrified. Someone saw a tall shape leave by the back. On the altar, in grey dust, someone has written one word, in a language nobody in {og_world} reads but you, somehow: Found.

choices.text: Rub out the word, and stay

effects.log: You rub it out. You stay with the congregation that winter. Nothing else comes. You keep watch anyway.

choices.text: Go after the tall shape

effects.log: You track it to a crossroads where the footprints stop. The air is cold. Nothing else is there.

choices.text: Help the congregation bury the priest

effects.log: You bury him with honour. Even the old temples send flowers.

events.text: In your dreams lately you stand on a wall of heaven, holding a broken sun, while a grey sea breaks below. You wake in your bed in {og_world} with your hands warm. Last night you woke to find someone standing at the foot of the bed: tall, faceless, watching. It bowed, and went out through the shutter as if the shutter were water.

choices.text: Hang a lamp at the foot of the bed

effects.log: You hang it. The light keeps the corners honest. The visitor does not come back. You think.

choices.text: Wait up for it the next night

effects.log: You wait up with a blade. It comes, sees you waiting, and goes. You feel you have passed a test.

choices.text: Move to a new house

effects.log: You move. The new house is smaller, and nothing stands at the foot of the bed.

events.text: Your strength is noticed in {og_world}, and lately it is noticed by the wrong eyes. A child at the market says a grey man asked her where you live. A hunter says something followed him home from the woods, asking for you. The wind at night has a new sound in it, like someone calling a name that is not yours, but was.

choices.text: Go into the woods and call it out

ok.log: It comes when you call. It is weaker than its voice. It goes back up into the sky with a sound like tearing silk.

fail.log: It comes, and it is stronger than its voice. You stagger home at dawn, alive, and it is still calling.

choices.text: Teach the village to keep their lamps lit

effects.log: You teach them. The village is bright at night now. The calling goes on, farther off.

events.text: The war in heaven over {og_world} has gone quiet. The sun is warm, the rivers run the right way, the hearth-fires burn orange. The priests say the gods are resting. In the taverns people have started a new toast, 'to quiet skies', and drink it with real feeling, the way people do when they have learned what the other kind is like.

choices.text: Raise a cup to the toast

effects.log: You raise your tea to it with a table of strangers. By the end of the night they are friends.

choices.text: Use the quiet to train

effects.log: You train while the sky is kind. It may not always be.

events.text: A famous troupe of players is touring the kingdoms of {og_world} with a new play: The Siege of Heaven. It is wildly wrong. The gods are played by actors on stilts. The grey things are played by children under a sheet. At the end the maker of the world comes on stage in a paper crown and wins, and the audience weeps every time.

choices.text: Go and see it, twice

effects.log: You see it twice. The second time you weep too, which surprises you.

choices.text: Offer the players silver for better stilts

effects.log: They buy better stilts. The play is less wrong. The audience still weeps.

events.text: In a quiet year, a scholar of the river kingdom publishes a book of everything the people of {og_world} saw during the war in heaven: the iron rain, the blue fires, the gods in the hayfields. She went to every kingdom and asked. She has dedicated it 'to the maker, who will want to know.' The book is very popular. She is very surprised.

choices.text: Read it cover to cover

effects.log: You read it in a week. It is a strange thing, to read your world's memory of you.

choices.text: Write to her with what you saw

effects.log: She puts your letter in the second edition, under 'a witness, unnamed'.

events.text: Children of {og_world} play a new game in the quiet years: one of them is the grey, one is the heaven, and the rest are the gods on the walls. The heaven always holds, in their game. When the grey child is caught, everyone goes to someone's mother for buns. You watch it from a doorway. One of the children waves you in to play the maker.

choices.text: Play the maker

effects.log: You play the maker. You are, the children agree, very good at it.

choices.text: Buy buns for everyone

effects.log: You buy the whole baker's tray. The game ends early, and nobody minds.

events.text: You sit on the walls of {og_heaven} in a quiet year and look down at {og_world}: its kingdoms, its rivers, its little lit towns. The grey is gone from between the heaven and the world. Your gods are at their posts, or asleep, or arguing about the weather. It is the quietest your heaven has ever been. You do not quite trust it.

choices.text: Trust it, for one evening

effects.log: You let yourself trust it. The evening is long and golden. Nothing comes.

choices.text: Walk the walls, and check every gate

effects.log: Every gate is sound. You check them twice. A god on watch pretends not to notice.

events.text: Every kingdom of {og_world} keeps a festival in midsummer called the Day the Hunger Died. Long ago, the stories say, a hungry thing from outside tried to eat all the heavens, and the one who made this world went out to the end of everything and killed it. The children make paper suns and break them in half, because the story says the maker carried a broken sun.

choices.text: Make a paper sun with the children

effects.log: You make one and break it in half. A child tells you that you broke it exactly right.

choices.text: Watch the procession from a roof

effects.log: You watch the broken suns go by. They look, from above, like a river of gold.

events.text: In the oldest temple of {og_world} there is a statue of the maker: no face, a broken sun in one hand, the other hand open, as if to someone just out of sight. The priests say the face was left blank so that anyone could be the maker, reborn. A pilgrim beside you looks at the statue, then at you, then at the statue again, and goes pale.

choices.text: Smile at the pilgrim

effects.log: You smile. The pilgrim bows very low and hurries away, and tells nobody, and remembers all their life.

choices.text: Lay your hand in the statue's open one

effects.log: You lay it there. The stone is warm. The priests see, and say nothing, and light a new lamp.

events.text: The storytellers of {og_world} have a saying when something good and unlikely happens: 'The maker walks among us.' Today a bridge in the river kingdom holds under a flood it should not have held under, because you put your shoulder to it at the right moment. The whole bank says it at once. You are soaked, and laughing, and you cannot explain why your eyes sting.

choices.text: Laugh it off and wring out your clothes

effects.log: You laugh. A woman brings you a dry coat. The saying follows you down the river.

choices.text: Stand on the bridge a while, quiet

effects.log: You stand. The flood goes by. The bridge holds. You hold too.

events.text: An old woman in a roadside inn of {og_world} tells you she was once a god of heaven, before the war, and that the maker saved them all. You have heard people say such things before. But she describes the maker's hands, and you look at your own, and she stops talking, and takes your hands in hers, and holds them, and says nothing at all for a long time.

choices.text: Let her hold them

effects.log: You let her. When she lets go, she says, 'Thank you,' and goes back to her fire, and is younger by a year.

choices.text: Ask her what the maker was like

effects.log: She says: tired, and kind, and stubborn. Like you. She laughs.
